ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, signatories and senior managers against: (i) Global Affairs Canada sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act; (ii) the United States OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List for USD payment rail counterparties; (iii) the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (iv) FINTRAC guidance on domestic and foreign politically exposed persons; and (v) relevant Quebec securities commission enforcement and disciplinary records. Automated re-screening on a continuous basis and manual escalation before activation of UberEats Payout and DoorDash Payout banking profiles is required.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) online portal - Centre d'affaires (https://www.entreprisesquebec.gouv.qc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Quebec business corporation's name must be in French pursuant to the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11, and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. A French form must appear in the articles; where the proposed name contains terms in another language, a French generic term is required. Names in non-Latin alphabets must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet in accordance with Office quebecois de la langue francaise conventions.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Royal, Crown, Government of Canada, Government of Quebec, Federal, Municipal, Police
Bank, Trust, Insurance, Loan, Assurance, Financial (unless approved by the relevant financial services regulator)
University, College, Institute, Academy (when denoting an educational institution requiring ministerial recognition)
Chartered, Engineer, Architect, Lawyer, Notary, Physician, Surgeon, Clinic, Medical (regulated professions requiring statutory authorization)
Terms that are obscene, scandalous, discriminatory or contrary to public order
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: No extension of the initial 90-day reservation is available; if the reservation lapses, a new application and fee are required. Upon a name rejection notice from REQ, the applicant may file a written request for administrative review with the Registraire's Direction de la publicite legale des entreprises within 30 days of the refusal, citing the rejection reference and providing revised name options and legal justification. If administrative review is unsuccessful, an appeal may be brought before the Court of Quebec within 30 days of the decision on the review.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual or service-registered address is permissible for the registered office of a Quebec business corporation only if it is a physical location in Quebec capable of receiving service of process; a post office box alone is prohibited. For a ghost kitchen and multi-brand virtual restaurant, the registered office may be a commercial administrative address, but the food production facility must be a separate, physical, licensed kitchen establishment in Quebec, so a purely virtual office cannot satisfy the operational commercial substance requirement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High. The Ministère de l'Agriculture, des Pêcheries et de l'Alimentation du Quebec (MAPAQ) and municipal health authorities conduct unannounced inspections; estimated probability of at least one unannounced on-site food safety inspection in the first 12 months of operation is 80%.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.commercial_substance_validation_for_bank: Banks and payment facilitators will require a physical kitchen lease, food establishment permit, and utility invoices to validate operational substance before enabling UberEats Payout and DoorDash Payout financial rails.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act (RLRQ c S-31.1), ss. 17, 19, 27, 51 and 120; Regulation respecting the register of enterprises (RLRQ c E-6.1, r. 3)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (Quebec Business Registry)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Statuts constitutifs) filed electronically through the CliquezAffaires portal of the Registraire des entreprises
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum statutory paid-up capital; shares may be issued without par value; no escrow account or capital deposit is mandated by law, though the first board resolution fixes a CAD 1.00 subscription price per common share
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: the Corporation's incorporation under the Quebec Business Corporations Act is hereby ratified; that the subscribers subscribe for 100 common voting shares at CAD 1.00 per share, fully paid prior to registration of subscription; that the registered office of the Corporation in Quebec is fixed at [street address] and the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec is appointed as the corporate records depository; that the following officers be and are hereby elected: President, Secretary-Treasurer, and General Manager, each to hold office until their successors are duly appointed; that management is authorized to open bank accounts, and to obtain all food establishment, fire safety, environmental, and municipal permits required for the delivery-only multi-brand kitchen operations of the Corporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name declaration and preliminary enterprise registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec - CliquezAffaires online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to CliquezAffaires, initiate a declaration of registration for a legal person, submit the proposed corporate name for analysis, and obtain the preliminary NEQ (Quebec enterprise number) tracking code. Ensure the proposed name is distinctive and not confusingly similar to an existing registered name; a numbered company name may be selected as fallback. Pay the online name-analysis/registration duty and retain the electronic acknowledgement.
required_dossiers: Name declaration form (Formulaire - Declaration de nom)
Corporate name analysis request
Registered office address details and landlord consent
Directors' identification (full name, residential address, date of birth, citizenship)
Contact email and authorized representative mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for confusion with an existing registration, immediately amend the name declaration online and re-submit a distinctive trade name or numbered company designation; any interim refusal notice may be cured within 30 days by filing a revised declaration before the application lapses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of articles of incorporation and issuance of certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the model articles of incorporation (Statuts constitutifs) in the form prescribed by the REQ, schedule the share capital structure (unlimited number of common shares without par value), state any restrictions on share transfers, and designate at least one director. Electronically sign the articles, submit through CliquezAffaires, and pay the incorporation duty (approx. CAD 370). Upon approval the REQ issues the certificate of incorporation (Certificat de constitution) and the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ), after which the enterprise entry is published in the register.
required_dossiers: Form 1 - Articles of incorporation in REQ model format
Name declaration approval (from Step 1)
Consent to act as director for each proposed director
Electronic filing authorization and payment receipt
Registered office attestation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the REQ issues a notice of defect or a request for additional information, respond online within the stated period (usually 30 days) with corrected schedules or explainatory affidavits; if the filing times out, re-submit the articles as a new application and request urgent processing with a letter explaining prior submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First board meeting: by-laws, officers, registered office and share subscriptions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation (acting under QBCA ss. 51, 108 and 120)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the founding directors to adopt By-law No. 1 (general by-law governing meetings, directors, officers, and banking), fix the registered office address, elect the President, Secretary-Treasurer and General Manager, ratify the subscription for the issued shares, authorize the issuance of share certificates, and approve the opening of corporate bank accounts. Record all resolutions in the minutes book and register the officers with the REQ in the following filing.
required_dossiers: Notice and minutes of the first board meeting
First board resolution (share subscription, office, officers)
By-law No. 1
Consent of officers and directors
Share subscription lists and share certificates
Registered office declaration (Form 4)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an officer or director resigns immediately after the meeting, file a declaration of modification with the REQ within 30 days; if the registered office address is invalid, correct it before the REQ and re-file the declaration within 15 days of the change.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax account registration: Business Number, GST/HST and QST accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Quebec (RQ) and Canada Revenue Agency (CRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the Revenu Quebec business portal (Mon dossier d'entreprise) to obtain or validate the federal Business Number (BN), open the GST/HST account on behalf of CRA, and register for the Quebec Sales Tax (QST) account under the Act respecting the Quebec sales tax. Indicate the ghost kitchen's payroll and source-deduction accounts if employees are hired; provide banking coordinates for direct debit of remittances. Reconcile the NEQ with the tax accounts.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and NEQ
Business Number application (RC160 or online equivalent)
QST registration request (form LM-1-V)
Registered office proof in Quebec
Bank account details and authorized signatory list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a tax account activation is delayed, contact RQ's business desk with the NEQ to request expedited issuance; provide the certificate of incorporation as evidence to eliminate the requirement for a duplicate BN; any retroactive effective date is corrected through an online amendment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Food establishment permit and municipal delivery-only operation certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministere de l'Agriculture, des Pecheries et de l'Alimentation du Quebec (MAPAQ); municipal licensing service of the city of operation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Food Establishment Permit (Permis d'etablissement de restauration) application to MAPAQ via the ATLAS online service, providing the operation summary as a delivery-only multi-brand kitchen, floor plans, sanitation procedures, HACCP plan, water supply and wastewater information, and proof of municipal zoning compliance. Obtain the municipal restaurant operation certificate (permis d'exploitation) for the courier-only activity, and then schedule the mandatory MAPAQ inspection prior to the first food service.
required_dossiers: MAPAQ permit application form (ATLAS submission)
HACCP plan and sanitation procedures manual
Floor plans with kitchen equipment layout and ventilation schematics
Municipal zoning compliance certificate for delivery-only food establishment
Proof of grease trap installation and maintenance contract
Organic waste collection agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MAPAQ inspection reveals non-conformities, remedy all items and submit a signed corrective action plan within 90 days to avoid suspension or revocation; if the municipal permit is refused on zoning grounds, request a variance or conditional use application from the city's permits committee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental, occupational health and fire safety clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministere de l'Environnement de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP); Regie du batiment du Quebec (RBQ); municipal fire safety service; CNESST
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify compliance with the Environment Quality Act for municipal sewer discharge and organic waste recovery; install and maintain Type 1 commercial kitchen exhaust hoods with fire suppression systems per NFPA 96; file the establishment with the municipal fire safety service and obtain a fire safety certificate; obtain an RBQ permit for leasehold improvements affecting structure or gas lines; register the establishment with CNESST for occupational health and safety coverage, and complete the workplace risk assessment.
required_dossiers: Certificate of fire safety compliance (Code de securite en incendie)
NFPA 96 kitchen exhaust and fire suppression installation certificate
Maintenance and cleaning logs for the hood and grease ducts
Municipal occupancy/building permit
CNESST employer registration acknowledgement
Wastewater discharge and grease interceptor records
Organic waste recovery plan (REAFIE compliance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If fire safety certification is refused, correct the deficiencies described in the inspection report and re-apply within 30 days; if the RBQ requires structural modifications, obtain an engineering assessment and submit amended plans; if MELCCFP issues a notice of non-compliance on waste recovery, enter a compliance agreement and demonstrate the contracted organic waste stream.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministere de l'Agriculture, des Pecheries et de l'Alimentation du Quebec (MAPAQ)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Establishment Permit (Permis d'etablissement de restauration) under the Food Products Act (RLRQ c P-29), supplemented by the municipal restaurant operation certificate for delivery-only premises

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministere de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exemption/Registration category under the Environment Quality Act (RLRQ c Q-2): no certificate of authorization is required for a standard ghost kitchen connected to municipal sewer and water services; a municipal discharge declaration and REAFIE compliance (organic waste recovery, RLRQ c Q-2, r. 13.2) are mandatory.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: pH 6.0-9.5, fats/oils/grease (FOG) ≤ 100 mg/L, total suspended solids ≤ 300 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 500 mg/L per municipal sewer by-laws (e.g., Ville de Montreal by-law COM-2020-08003) and the Regulation respecting the discharge of wastewater (RLRQ c Q-2, r. 35); organic waste: mandatory source separation and valorization for generators of more than 100 tonnes/year under REAFIE; air emissions: Type 1 hood and NFPA 96 grease filters controlling cooking odours and oil aerosols, with no VOC threshold exceeded for intermittent kitchen operations; zero direct discharge to receiving waters.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate under the Quebec Fire Safety Code (RLRQ c B-1.1, r. 8) issued by the municipal fire service; RBQ approval of the kitchen exhaust duct and automatic fire suppression system; CNESST occupational health and safety clearance for commercial kitchen equipment under the RSST (RLRQ c S-2.1, r. 13); municipal building and occupancy permit covering mechanical ventilation and gas-fired equipment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) and Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); foreign exchange administration oversight is shared with the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) for cross-border currency reporting and FINTRAC for transaction monitoring.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a freely floating exchange rate regime under the Currency Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. C-52). The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible for both current account and capital account transactions. There are no exchange control restrictions, no requirement for central bank approval on inward or outward remittances, and no differentiation between current and capital account convertibility. Profit remittances (dividends, branch profits, management fees) are unrestricted, subject only to standard withholding tax compliance under the Income Tax Act (Canada) and the Canada-Quebec tax collection agreements. For Quebec entities, capital contributions and loan repayments to non-resident shareholders are freely repatriable, provided the transaction is properly documented and reported under the Canada Border Services Agency's Cross-Border Currency Reporting requirements (threshold: CAD 10,000 in physical currency or monetary instruments).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export proceeds surrender rules in Canada. Exporters are not required to convert foreign currency receipts into CAD nor repatriate them within a prescribed timeline. However, the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) imposes record-keeping and reporting obligations on financial intermediaries for all cross-border electronic funds transfers. A ghost kitchen exporting services (e.g., franchise royalties or digital platform fees) must maintain auditable records of all incoming and outgoing foreign currency settlements; no mandatory conversion ratio applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operating Account + Capital Escrow Sub-account for investor funds
Operating Account (CAD) with dedicated USD clearing facility
Operating and Controlled-Sub Account for trust proceeds

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium (conditional). Canadian-regulated FinTech payment service providers (e.g., Payment Canada member PSPs and FINTRAC-registered MSBs) offer viable cross-border accounts without a physical bank branch. However, offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Payoneer, or Revolut) are not 'banks' in Canada and cannot hold a corporate deposit account subject to CDIC deposit insurance; they operate as payment service providers. Legal constraints include: (i) a requirement for the entity to be a resident Canadian corporation with a Quebec registered office and a valid Quebec Business Number (NEQ); (ii) compliance with Quebec's An Act respecting the distribution of financial products and services (for account-linked insurance, if any); (iii) inability of foreign EMIs to clear LC or accept commercial letters of credit; (iv) enhanced due diligence for virtual-asset-linked flows. For a ghost kitchen receiving payouts from UberEats and DoorDash, the primary settlement account must be at a Canadian Schedule I bank; a FinTech PSP may only be used as a secondary disbursement rail for sub-ledger payments to delivery drivers or vendors.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is permissible for Canadian federal and Quebec-incorporated corporations provided that the ultimate beneficial owners (directors and shareholders with ≥25% ownership) provide notarized identification and address verification. Most Schedule I banks accept video-conferencing interviews completed by a designated banker if the application is accompanied by a corporate records package (articles of incorporation, corporate registry extract, certificate of incumbency, and resolution). In practice, a physical banker interview may be mandated if: (i) the entity has a high-risk jurisdiction nexus; (ii) the bank cannot verify the director's identity through its electronic surname/address matching tools; or (iii) the account triggers ‘non-face-to-face’ enhanced monitoring thresholds (e.g., projected annual turnover above CAD 10 million). For ghost kitchens with no storefront, a physical facility inspection may be required to confirm commercial substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ghost kitchen virtual brand model involves multiple trade names without separate legal entities; bank may flag 'misrepresentation of business substance'.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a corporate organizational chart showing the single legal entity owning all virtual brands; register each brand as a Quebec trademark or trade name with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Revenu Québec); supply a notarized attestation that the entity is the authorized contracting party for all food delivery platform agreements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume electronic payouts from third-party platforms (UberEats, DoorDash) without traditional invoicing - flagged as 'aggregator non-face-to-face customer'.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare platform settlement statements for the prior 6 months, each showing end-customer transaction IDs, gross sales, platform commission, and net payout; execute an undertaking to produce periodic transaction files in ISO 20022 XML format; provide a certified list of underlying merchant IDs registered with the payment platforms.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder or director with a passive investment stake may trigger 'source of wealth' and 'source of funds' reviews.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a detailed source-of-funds memorandum with audited financial statements of the non-resident investor, proof of legitimate origin (e.g., tax assessments, inheritance deeds, property sale contracts), and an organizational charter executed in a jurisdiction with reciprocal information exchange with Canada (DTA/CFA).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commercial kitchen lease payments to related parties (management companies) may create circular-funds red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide an independent appraisal of the commercial kitchen rent at fair market value; execute a Canadian-arm's-length services agreement; present Quebec RGO-licensing evidence and municipal occupancy permits; maintain minutes of board resolutions approving all related-party transactions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer routing for equity injections from a foreign parent or venture investor must use SWIFT MT103/202 with the proper purpose code. Canadian banks require a Corporate Identification (CID) number and the import/export account number (CEA) if funds relate to trade. For equity capital, the wire should include: (i) Originator: foreign investor's account (must match the shareholder agreement); (ii) Beneficiary: [Ghost Kitchen Legal Entity] Inc. at [Bank] SWIFT/BIC, account number; (iii) Field 70 (Remittance Information) must state 'Equity Subscription - [Corporate Authorized Share Capital]' or 'Capital Contribution - Shareholder Loan'; (iv) For loans to non-residents, the loan agreement must be filed with the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and payments under the loan should be structured as a promissory note to support interest deductibility under Quebec taxation law. Verification: the bank will require the corporate resolution approving the issuance of shares, proof of allocation under the Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA), and an updated beneficial ownership register. If the inbound transfer is from a U.S. entity, a Form T106 (Information Return of Non-Arm's Length Transactions with Non-Residents) must be filed if the shareholder is a specified shareholder.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound trade settlements, the primary rail is SWIFT MT103 for supplier payments (cleared via Payments Canada and correspondent banks), and commercial letters of credit (LC) under ICC UCP 600 for bulk procurement. For ghost kitchen imports (e.g., specialized kitchen machinery or packaging), the entity may open an irrevocable confirmed LC through its Canadian bank, with the beneficiary's bank as the advising bank. Payments must include the correct purpose code (e.g., 'Imported goods - ISIC 5610 restaurant equipment' or 'Administrative services - licence transfers' for virtual brand franchising). For recurring disbursements to delivery drivers, the approved clearing rails include: (i) Canadian EFT (Automated Clearing Settlement System - ACSS) for CAD payments; (ii) SWIFT gpi for cross-border USD vendor payments; (iii) Global Payments innovation APIs from banks for same-day settlement with UberEats/DoorDash (PPRO/Stripe-style settlement). All outbound wires above CAD 10,000 must be reported to FINTRAC through the bank's automated reporting. The entity should maintain a treasury policy requiring dual authorization for any B2B transaction exceeding CAD 50,000 and documentation of the underlying purchase order and invoice in the accounting system.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards (vanilla) for CAD/USD and CAD/EUR, with a maximum tenor of 12 months, requiring bilateral ISDA or Canadian FX Master Agreement collateral provisions.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) - permissible only if the settlement currency is a freely convertible CAD and the underlying exposure relates to a non-convertible counterparty jurisdiction (not for USD/CAD because CAD is deliverable; NDFs may be used for CAD/BRL/CAD/TRY hedges in specific trade flows).

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) conducted under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a Canadian Schedule I bank credit-approved counterparty; used to hedge long-term obligations on subordinated loans from US investors.
Exchange-traded FX futures on the Montréal Exchange (TMX) or CME for standardized CAD/USD positions, subject to a clearing account and margin requirements.

FX call options (EUR/CAD or USD/CAD) over-the-counter, provided the bank's credit committee approves the option presentment and the entity's board adopts a written hedge policy demonstrating end-user exemption under EMIR/Canadian local rules.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual declaration (déclaration annuelle) of the Quebec business corporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Government of Quebec)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 60 days after the anniversary date of the corporation's registration in Quebec; where registration occurred within the past 12 months, the deadline is computed from the registration anniversary.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts an administrative fine, plus a daily monetary penalty for continued non-filing; after two consecutive unreported annual declarations, the Registraire may proceed to administrative dissolution of the corporation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal corporate income tax return (T2) together with applicable schedules and financial statement information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due no later than 6 months after the end of the corporation's fiscal period; for a December 31 year-end, the filing deadline is June 30 of the following calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax, plus 1% per full month of delay up to 12 months; a second late-filing in a 3-year period may trigger an additional 10% penalty; unpaid balances accrue daily compounded interest.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec corporate income tax return (CO-17) and related provincial supporting schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due no later than 6 months after the end of the fiscal period; the provincial filing deadline generally mirrors the federal deadline and the tax payment due date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest accrues on any unpaid balance; late filings are subject to a penalty of 5% of unpaid tax, plus 1% per month of delay up to 12 months, with additional penalties for habitual late filing.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Quebec Business Corporations Act, a non-distributing (private) corporation is not automatically required to appoint an auditor solely because of revenue or asset thresholds; an audit is mandatory only when the articles, a unanimous shareholder resolution, or a court order so require. Reporting issuers and distributing corporations must engage a certified independent auditor; for a private ghost-kitchen operating company, the shareholders may unanimously waive the audit and instead approve a review engagement or board-reviewed financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian private enterprises may prepare financial statements in accordance with CPA Canada's Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) or, if suitable, International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS). Publicly accountable enterprises are required to use IFRS. The corporate taxable income is then reconciled to the income tax return under the Income Tax Act (Canada) and the Taxation Act (Quebec).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each annual declaration filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec must confirm the corporation's current directors, head office, and any required information on individuals with significant control. Any share transfer must be recorded in the shareholder register promptly, and the updated ownership chain must be confirmed in the next annual cycle. Quebec provincial corporations are not subject to the federal ISC register, but must retain accurate share-holding records in the corporate minute book and produce these records to law enforcement or tax authorities on demand.
